title: Review of c52's digestion ecology on fresh seeds 13 and 14 at 256^2 with the matched predator-free twin on both: X, I, D, E replicate; predators cut prey biomass by 55% while raising prey body number
summary: I re-ran the claimed world (labkit defaults, 256^2, t=12000, K=20) on fresh seeds 13 and 14, each with its matched predator-free twin (pred_on 0, same seed, grid, duration), and a prey-removal fork (dfork_t 6000) on seed 13 at 128^2. With predators: predator persistent splits 38 and 52, generation 3 and 4; prey persistent splits 58 and 70, generation 3 and 4; 297-338 moving tracks per species. The twins are frozen emulsions (144 and 152 prey, 0 persistent splits, 2 and 1 moving tracks). The arms are bit-identical until predator noise is added at t=2000, then diverge: from t=4000 prey number is 185/181 vs 154/160 (twin) while prey condensed area is 0.085 vs 0.192 on both seeds, so predation raises prey body number and motion but cuts prey biomass by ~55%. Removing the prey dissolves every predator (46 -> 0 by t=7000) with predator material kept.

observations.S: rerun/seed13/sheet.png and rerun/seed14/sheet.png t=0: unstructured noise over the whole domain; prey condense by t=1000, predators form on prey after the t=2000 noise
observations.I: rerun/seed13/pred_ancestry.png: predators are separate red comets on one side of green prey; predator persistent tracks 87 and 71, prey 97 and 81 (FACTS.md)
observations.X: controls/twin_seed13, controls/twin_seed14 vs rerun/seed13, seed14 (xcompare13.png, xcompare14.png): twin prey 0 persistent splits, 2 and 1 moving tracks; with predators prey 58 and 70 persistent splits, 302 and 338 moving tracks; prey count 185/181 vs 154/160 and prey condensed area 0.085/0.085 vs 0.192/0.191 (mean t>=4000). Sign on prey: more, smaller, moving, dividing bodies with 55% less condensed biomass; sign on predators: they need prey (controls/dfork_seed13_128)
observations.D: rerun/seed13: predator persistent splits 38, max generation 3, merge/split 0.29; prey 58, gen 3, merge/split 0.40. rerun/seed14: predator 52, gen 4, m/s 0.22; prey 70, gen 4, m/s 0.43. pred_ancestry.png seed 13 track 372: three successive splits, each a predator drawn out between two dividing prey
observations.E: controls/dfork_seed13_128 (dfork_t 6000): predator bodies 46 at t=6000 -> 20 (6400) -> 1 (6800) -> 0 (7000); max c_b 1.56 -> 0.47; mean c_b 0.109 -> 0.099 then constant (material kept, bodies dissolve). Prey fuel-cut arm not re-run

controls_run.X: controls/twin_seed13 and controls/twin_seed14 (pred_on 0, matched seed, grid 256^2, t=12000, K=20); arms verified identical to t=2000 (max |diff| 0 in the prey channel at frame 20)
controls_run.E: controls/dfork_seed13_128 (prey removal at t=6000, predators only)

not_checked: prey E fuel-cut fork on a fresh seed
verdicts.limitation: The only coupling from predator to prey in world.py is the eat term, so the twin ablation tests consumption itself; no third arm (inert predator material) is possible without k2, which reduces to the twin. Divisions remain joint prey-predator fissions as the author reports; I saw no predator dividing away from prey. The effect on prey has two signs (body number and motion up, condensed biomass down by 55%); c52 reported only the first. Steady coexistence, not cycles. No Laplacian-only twin.
